items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee responds to the interviewer's statement about Dick 'Ricardo' Sugar's radio show and Tico recordings with a general comment about the music industry ('It's like you playing baseball...'), indicating awareness of Sugar's role but no personal interaction or professional relationship des

ctx.x: Now, Dick 'Ricardo' Sugar became -- had a fifteen-minute show on WHBI in September, 1948. By the end of the year he had a few Tico recordings of Al Castellanos and then in 1949 he got those recordings of Tito Puente, like "Abaniquito" and "Maina Go" and "La Renta" by Tito Rodriguez; and he would only play those on the Tico and I heard they didn't play Machito or no one else, except those Tico recordings and they didn't start playing you steady until you got on the Tico label. Doesn't that tell you anything?

Yeah, but how could you - I mean fight the, the whatever. It's just a matter you have to be in the -- It's like you playing baseball and you sitting on the bench and somebody with less quality he is playing regularly and you're sitting on the bench.
